# Draft:Our Own High School, Al Warqa

| website        =
}}
Our Own High School, Al Warqa (OOW) is a private, all-boys school in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Established in 2005, the school is a member of the GEMS Education network and follows the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) curriculum of India.
The school is a branch of the historic Our Own English High School (established in 1968). It was opened as a purpose-built, single-shift facility to accommodate the male student population from the original campus.
History
The school traces its legacy to the founding of the first GEMS school in Bastakiya by K.S. Varkey and Mariama Varkey. In 2005, the Al Warqa campus was inaugurated as a dedicated boys' school. Over the decades, it has evolved into one of the largest Indian-curriculum schools for boys in the region.
Campus and Facilities
Located in Al Warqa 1, the campus includes:
* Eight ICT laboratories and specialized Science labs.
* A 600-seat multipurpose auditorium.
* Sports infrastructure including an AstroTurf field, basketball courts, and cricket nets.
* A "Mathematics Lab" and an environmental activity room for hands-on learning.
Academics
The school follows the CBSE curriculum from Grade 1 through Grade 12. In the Senior Secondary phase (Grades 11 and 12), students can choose between Science and Commerce streams.
KHDA Inspection
The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) has rated the school as "Good" for over ten consecutive years (2011–2026). Recent reports highlight "Outstanding" performance in student personal and social development, as well as community and environmental responsibility.
Awards and Achievements
Environmental Awards
The school is a prominent recipient of sustainability honors in the UAE:
* Sharjah Environmental Awareness Award (2016): Won first place for the "Forest with Recyclable Materials" project.
* DEWA Conservation Award (2017): Named winner in the "Distinguished Conservation Team" category.
Sports and Robotics
* Robotics: The school was the first winner of the UAE National Robotics Olympiad in 2006. Its teams have represented the UAE at the World Robot Olympiad in countries including China, Japan, and South Korea.
* Cricket and Athletics: The school holds multiple titles in the Maxtalent Global Vision Cup and consistently qualifies for the CBSE National Athletic Meets.
